title: Rethinking Verification in Agent Harnesses
abstract: arXiv:2610.34577v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent harnesses enable large language models to act through tools, observe the results, and iteratively work toward a task goal. Verification checks and revises agents' work to improve output quality. Yet there is limited guidance on how harnesses should organize this effort. We study verification as an axis of test-time scaling by examining when to intervene, who checks the work, and how checking leads to revision. Our framework spans four layers of the agent lifecycle: initial instructions, mid-turn reminders, completion gates, and independent review. We compare 17 designs across seven frontier coding models on Terminal-Bench (TB) and SWE-bench Verified (SWE), and introduce VisualBench for expert evaluation of visual and interactive artifacts. Initial instructions and execution-time reminders yield modest, model-dependent average gains on the coding benchmarks, without substantially increasing average output token use. Completion gates

translated_title: 重新思考智能体框架中的验证机制
translated_abstract: 智能体框架使大语言模型能够通过工具执行操作、观察结果，并迭代地朝任务目标推进。验证通过检查和修订智能体的工作来提升输出质量，然而关于框架应如何组织这项工作，目前仍缺乏指导。我们将验证作为测试时扩展的一个维度加以研究，考察何时介入、由谁检查工作、以及检查如何引发修订。我们的框架覆盖智能体生命周期的四个层次：初始指令、执行中途提醒、完成门控和独立审查。我们在Terminal-Bench（TB）和SWE-bench Verified（SWE）上比较了七种前沿编码模型下的17种设计，并引入VisualBench用于对视觉与交互式产物进行专家评估。初始指令和执行时提醒在编码基准上带来了适度的、因模型而异的平均收益，且不会显著增加平均输出token用量。完成门控（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将验证作为测试时扩展的新维度，系统考察智能体框架中验证的介入时机、检查者与修订机制，覆盖智能体生命周期四个层次并在多个基准上比较了17种设计，同时引入VisualBench用于评估视觉与交互式产物。
en_tdlr: This paper rethinks verification in agent harnesses as an axis of test-time scaling, systematically examining when to intervene, who checks, and how checking drives revision across four layers of the agent lifecycle, comparing 17 designs on coding benchmarks and introducing VisualBench for expert evaluation of visual and interactive artifacts.
